clinician.final_diagnosis: Stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma with metastases to the liver and lung
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 29-year-old African American male with 5 years of daily alcohol use presented to the ED with right upper quadrant abdominal pain and early satiety. Initial CT imaging revealed a 14 cm mass in the left lobe of the liver with hepatomegaly and mildly elevated transaminases (ALT 51, AST 74, ALP 93). The patient was discharged with planned outpatient hepatology follow-up. At 10-week readmission, CT of the neck with contrast identified a 6.5 cm complex bilobed mass in the right parotid gland. Biopsy of the parotid mass demonstrated a well-differentiated carcinoma with distinctive myxoid stroma, tubular and cribriform structures, and immunohistochemistry findings suggestive of adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC), though BCAC could not be completely excluded without complete tumor examination. Chest CT at 2 months after initial presentation revealed innumerable bilateral pulmonary nodules measuring up to 8 mm, favoring metastases. The parotid gland mass was identified as the primary tumor site with documented metastatic disease to the liver and lungs, establishing stage IV adenoid cystic carcinoma. Given the tremendous tumor burden and poor prognosis, palliative chemotherapy with cisplatin and vinorelbine was initiated.
